bib.title: An Image is Worth One Word: Personalizing Text-to-Image Generation using Textual Inversion

question: How can a frozen text-to-image model be made to generate a user-provided concept (object or style) in new scenes, using only 3-5 example images?
hypothesis: A single new word embedding, optimised with a visual reconstruction objective in the frozen text encoder's embedding space, can capture a unique concept while keeping it editable by natural language.
contributions: Introduce the task of personalized text-to-image generation
Present Textual Inversion: learn pseudo-words in the text-encoder embedding space that capture high-level semantics and fine visual details
Analyze the embedding space with GAN-inversion-inspired techniques and show a distortion-editability tradeoff
Evaluate against human-caption baselines, showing higher visual fidelity and more robust editing

method.summary: Optimise one new token embedding v* (placeholder S*) with the LDM denoising loss on 3-5 images of a concept, with neutral CLIP ImageNet templates as prompts, while the autoencoder, text encoder and denoiser stay frozen. The learned word is then used inside ordinary prompts.
method.task: personalized text-to-image generation via embedding inversion

datasets.name: Concept image sets (user-provided)
datasets.size: 3-5 images per concept (typically); 1 to 25 swept in Appendix B
datasets.source: Authors' concepts; some artist images used with permission for non-commercial use

datasets.name: LAION-400M
datasets.source: Schuhmann et al., 2021; used to pretrain the LDM

datasets.name: Mechanical Turk captions
datasets.size: 10 captions per concept (5 short <=12 words, 5 long <=30 words)
datasets.source: Annotators saw four images and described the concept so an artist could recreate it

models.name: Latent Diffusion Model (Rombach et al., 2021)
models.architecture: latent diffusion with BERT text encoder

other.frozen: text encoder c_theta and denoiser eps_theta fixed; only v* trained

training.objective: LDM loss (Eq. 2): E ||eps - eps_theta(z_t, t, c_theta(y))||^2 minimised over v* only
training.lr: base 0.005, scaled by GPUs and batch size to effective 0.04

other.init: embedding of a single-word coarse descriptor (e.g. 'sculpture', 'cat')
other.other_hparams: original LDM hyperparameters retained unless noted
other.templates: 27 neutral templates in Appendix D; style concepts use 'A painting in the style of S*'
other.caveat: for some concepts fewer steps or higher lr work better

inference.decoding: LDM sampling; 50 DDIM steps in the evaluation
inference.samples: 64 images per concept per prompt for CLIP metrics; 16 candidates (6 for DALLE-2) per prompt, best manually chosen for qualitative figures
inference.prompting: Prompts containing S*, e.g. 'A photo of S* on the moon'

parameters.guidance_scale: LDM typical 5-10 mentioned; Fig 11 uses s=1,2,5

metrics.name: Reconstruction
metrics.definition: Average pairwise CLIP-space cosine similarity between 64 images generated with 'A photo of S*' and the concept training images

metrics.name: Editability
metrics.definition: Cosine similarity between mean CLIP embedding of 64 samples and CLIP embedding of the prompt with S* removed

metrics.name: User study ranking
metrics.definition: Users rank outputs of five models by similarity to training images or to the text

baselines: Human captions (short and long) with LDM
DALLE-2 with image input and captions
PALAVRA with VQGAN-CLIP and Guided Diffusion
CLIP Guided Diffusion with init image
Image Only and Prompt Only reference setups
eval.protocol: Single-concept CLIP scores per setup (Fig 10a, values only in figure); user study 600 responses per questionnaire, 1,200 total, 95% CI error bars.

availability.weights: new words will be available (same site)

prompts.purpose: Training templates (first and last of list)

prompts.text: A painting in the style of S∗

evidence.quote: The base learning rate was set to 0.005.

results.claim: Learning one concept takes about two hours with the stated setup.
results.quote: learning a single concept requires roughly two hours

results.claim: Training uses 5,000 steps at effective lr 0.04.
results.quote: All results were produced using 5, 000 optimization steps.

results.claim: User study collected 1,200 responses in total.
results.quote: collected a total of 600 responses to each questionnaire, for a total of 1, 200 responses

results.claim: Best results with about 5 training images; more images move the embedding away from real-word embeddings and hurt editability.
results.quote: Our method operates best when provided with 5 images.

results.claim: Single-word embedding gives reconstruction comparable to multi-word baselines and better editability.
results.setup: CLIP metrics, Fig 10(a); numbers only in figure
results.quote: the single-word method achieves comparable recon- struction quality, and considerably improved editability over all multi-word baselines
results.note: no numeric scores in text; text spans a line break so verify quote

results.claim: Human captions fail to capture likeness and reduce editability.
results.setup: Short and long MTurk captions with LDM
results.quote: the use of human descriptions for the concepts not only fails to capture their likeness, but also leads to diminished editability

results.claim: Learning rate moves the single-word model along the distortion-editability curve.
results.quote: our single-embedding model can be moved along this curve by simply changing the learning rate

limits: Struggles with precise shapes; captures semantic essence (Sec 6)
Lengthy optimisation, about two hours per concept (Sec 6)
Fails at relations between multiple learned concepts, e.g. side-by-side (Sec 4.4)
CLIP metrics are insensitive to shape preservation (Sec 5.3)
Qualitative results are partially curated (best of 16)
Only evaluated on LDM 1.4B; larger models are conjecture
Fig 10 scores are only in figures, no table of numbers
Numbers: no seeds or variance reported; optimizer not named

terms.definition: A new embedding vector v* with placeholder string S*, treated like any other word in prompts
Finding a pseudo-word embedding via optimization so that 'A photo of S*' reconstructs the concept images

lineage.note: Compared with image inputs and captions

lineage.work: Designing an encoder for StyleGAN image manipulation (Tov et al.)
